methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/NS.json), cross-verified against the real chapter table of contents and raw page images (pdftoppm renders of 'Toronto Notes 2025.pdf', pdf pages 933-986) given this chapter's severe two-column TOC OCR corruption: 32 of 47 toc_inventory.json source nodes carried LOW/MEDIUM packet-extraction confidence. Page-image review of the chapter TOC (pdf 933) and targeted body pages (pdf 934, 936, 939, 940-941, 944, 977) confirmed the underlying corruption is column-bleed: OCR text from an adjacent TOC column or a nearby unrelated heading was appended to, or substituted for, the genuine heading text, in several distinct patterns: (1) genuine multi-word headings with trailing garbage appended, matching a real heading elsewhere in the chapter whose text bled across columns (e.g. NS.S02.T02 'ICP/Volume Relationship Nou louie i 5 orn ined Death' = real 'ICP/Volume Relationship' + bled fragment of 'Neurologically Determined Death'; NS.S02.T03 'Cerebral Blood Flow Come ogically Determined Dea' = real 'Cerebral Blood Flow' + further bleed of the same 'Neurologically Determined Death' heading; NS.S02.T05 'Elevated ICP Persistent Vegetative State' = real 'Elevated ICP' + bled 'Persistent Vegetative State' heading text; NS.S03.T01 'Treatment of Elevated ICP Spinal Dysraphism' = real 'Treatment of Elevated ICP' + bled 'Spinal Dysraphism'; NS.S03.T03 'Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumour Cerebri) . Hydrocephalus in Pediatrics' = real standalone heading 'Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumour Cerebri)' [confirmed via body-page review, pdf 940-941/NS8-9] + bled 'Hydrocephalus in Pediatrics'); (2) a genuine heading split/truncated across two sibling nodes (NS.S10.T01 'Arteriovenous Malformations, Cavernous Malformations, and' + NS.S10.T02 'Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas' are one real TOC heading 'Arteriovenous Malformations, Cavernous Malformations, and Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas', split by a column break); (3) a spurious extra child node with no matching body content at its assigned page location (NS.S02.T01 'Head Injury' - no such heading exists on pdf 936-938/NS4-6, confirmed via body-page review; the real 'Head Injury' heading is a sub-bullet of Neurotrauma at NS35/pdf967, already captured within NS.S15 - T01 is treated as a duplicate artifact, not an independent study unit; similarly NS.S03.T02 'Intraventricular Hemorrhage' has no matching content at pdf939-940/NS7-8, its real content being the Pediatric Neurosurgery IVH sub-bullet at NS41/NS.S15; and NS.S04.T01 'Craniosynostosis' has no matching content at pdf941-942/NS9-10, its real content being the Pediatric Neurosurgery Craniosynostosis sub-bullet at NS43/NS.S15 - both are represented as their own study units sourced from NS.S15's page span, with the duplicate/misplaced T-node id retained in source_node_ids for traceability); (4) four section-level nodes (NS.S16-NS.S19) whose titles are entirely OCR noise unrelated to their actual body content: page-image review confirmed pdf 944/NS12 (node NS.S06, titled 'CNS Tumours') actually contains ALL SIX CNS tumour subtopics listed in the real TOC (Metastatic Tumours, Adult Diffuse Gliomas, Primary CNS Lymphoma, Meningioma, Vestibular Schwannoma, Pituitary Adenoma) as body content spanning pdf944-950/NS12-18, while pdf 977/NS45 (node NS.S16, titled 'Metastatic Tumours Movement Disorders') actually contains the genuine 'Functional Neurosurgery' > 'Movement Disorders' and 'Chronic Pain' body content (confirmed via body-page review) - the CNS-tumour-subtopic-sounding titles on NS.S16/S17/S18/S19 are column-bleed duplicates of the NS.S06 subtopic names, not independent content; the real content at those page positions is Functional Neurosurgery (NS.S16, pdf977/NS45), Surgical Management of Epilepsy (NS.S17, pdf978/NS46), Surgical Management of Trigeminal Neuralgia (NS.S18, pdf979/NS47), and Landmark Neurosurgery Trials (NS.S19, pdf980-983/NS48-51) per the real chapter TOC - this is the same 'title from OCR noise unrelated to actual body content' pattern documented for N.S27 in the Neurology chapter precedent, and is resolved the same way: the node_id is retained for traceability and its REAL, TOC-confirmed body content is used for the study unit derived from it, while its corrupted title text is not used to derive a topic. One organizational section header could not be page-anchored with sufficient confidence and is recorded, per project instruction, as UNRESOLVED rather than guessed: the packet's source_quality.unresolved_headings entry for 'INTRACRANIAL PATHOLOGY' (a non-clinical organizational divider at NS4/pdf933-934, distinct from the clinical content around it, which IS resolved). No toc_inventory.json node was found to be entirely missing from the pipeline's output; every real heading traces to an existing, if sometimes mistitled or misplaced, node_id, used directly for traceability with the correction documented in each affected study unit's structural_rationale. No corruption was resolved from neurosurgical background knowledge; every correction traces to the rendered pdf page images listed above or to the packet's own merged_duplicate_headings/toc_inventory.json fields. Two organizational/non-clinical portions are excluded from study units, consistent with N/ID/MI/NP chapter precedent: the chapter-opening abbreviation glossary (part of NS.S01, alongside genuine 'Basic Anatomy Review' content) and the closing References section (NS.S20).
organizational_header_nodes: NS.S02 (INTRACRANIAL PATHOLOGY portion - UNRESOLVED page anchor)

study_units.title: Basic Anatomy Review
study_units.structural_rationale: toc_inventory node NS.S01 is titled 'Acronyms' but its merged_duplicate_headings field records 'Basic Anatomy Review' as co-located content on the same page (pdf 934/NS2), confirmed via raw page-image review: pdf p.934 contains the abbreviation glossary followed by a substantial 'Basic Anatomy Review' section (surface anatomy, MRI neuroanatomy figures). The non-clinical acronym glossary is excluded from study units, consistent with N/ID/MI/NP chapter precedent for chapter-opening abbreviation lists; only the genuine Basic Anatomy Review content is represented here.

study_units.title: Differential Diagnoses of Common Presentations (Intracranial/Spinal/Peripheral Lesions)
study_units.structural_rationale: Confirmed via body-page review (pdf 936/NS4): a standalone 'Differential Diagnoses of Common Presentations' table (Table 1) covering intracranial mass lesions, disorders of the spine, and peripheral nerve lesions, distinct from the 'Intracranial Pressure Dynamics' content that follows on the same page (represented separately as SU-NS-03). This organizing differential table frames but does not itself carry independently testable content beyond what is captured in the disease-specific units below.

study_units.title: Intracranial Pressure Dynamics (ICP/Volume Relationship, Cerebral Blood Flow, ICP Measurement, Elevated ICP)
study_units.structural_rationale: NS.S02.T02-T05 are OCR-garbled versions of the four real sub-bullets of 'Intracranial Pressure Dynamics' (ICP/Volume Relationship, Cerebral Blood Flow, ICP Measurement, Elevated ICP) confirmed against the real chapter TOC (pdf 933) and body-page review (pdf 936-937, Table 2 'Approach to Intracranial Pathology' and Table 4 'Clinical Features of Elevated ICP'); each carries a bled fragment of a distant heading ('Neurologically Determined Death' bled into T02/T03, 'Persistent Vegetative State' bled into T05) which is stripped as noise, not treated as separate content. A fifth sibling node, NS.S02.T01 'Head Injury', is a spurious duplicate with no matching body content anywhere on pdf 936-938/NS4-6 (the real 'Head Injury' heading is a Neurotrauma sub-bullet at NS35, already captured in SU-NS-33) and is therefore excluded from this unit's source_node_ids.

study_units.structural_rationale: Matches the real chapter TOC directly; confirmed via body-page review (pdf 939/NS7, Table 5 'Herniation Syndromes' covering subfalcine, central tentorial, uncal, upward, and tonsillar herniation).
